metadata.name: mkfs
metadata.version: util-linux (mkfs is a front-end; mkfs.ext4, etc.)

installation.note: mkfs is a front-end; mkfs.ext4, mkfs.xfs, etc. are in e2fsprogs, xfsprogs, etc.

overview.summary: mkfs (make filesystem) creates a filesystem on a partition or device. It is a front-end: mkfs.ext4 runs mke2fs, mkfs.xfs runs mkfs.xfs, etc. This erases existing data on the device. Use with extreme care.
when_to_use: Format a new partition with ext4, xfs, or other type

syntax.description: DEVICE is the partition (e.g., /dev/sdb1). TYPE can be ext4, xfs, btrfs, etc. Often invoked as mkfs.ext4 DEVICE.

options.description: Specify filesystem type (ext4, xfs, btrfs, vfat, etc.)

examples.title: Format as XFS
examples.use_case: XFS for large files or performance

common_pitfalls.description: Formatting the wrong partition destroys all data on it.
common_pitfalls.solution: Confirm device with lsblk or fdisk -l; never format the system root or data you need.

related_commands.description: Partition first; then mkfs to format
Mount the new filesystem after mkfs
